📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough The operator now reads the cluster APIServer TLS security profile at startup and passes it through runtime-extractor reconciliation. DaemonSet application now derives and appends kube-rbac-proxy TLS cipher-suite and minimum-version arguments from that profile, with tests covering the new behavior. ## Changes **TLS profile wiring for runtime-extractor** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Startup TLS profile fetch**
`pkg/controller/operator.go`|Adds `configv1` import, fetches the APIServer cluster TLS profile during `Operator.Run`, and passes it into `NewRuntimeExtractorController`.| |**Controller TLS propagation**
`pkg/controller/runtimeextractor/controller.go`|Adds TLS profile storage to the controller, updates the constructor signature, and threads the stored profile through create, update, and drift reconciliation calls to `ApplyRuntimeExtractorResources`.| |**DaemonSet TLS args**
`pkg/controller/runtimeextractor/resources/manager.go`, `pkg/controller/runtimeextractor/resources/daemonset.go`|Updates `ApplyRuntimeExtractorResources` and `applyDaemonSet` to accept a TLS profile, derives kube-rbac-proxy TLS args from the profile, and appends them to the matching container while using the kube-rbac-proxy container name constant in image updates.| |**TLS argument tests**
`pkg/controller/runtimeextractor/resources/daemonset_test.go`, `pkg/controller/runtimeextractor/resources/retry_test.go`|Adjusts existing tests for the new signatures and adds coverage for TLS arg generation and injection across profile variants. | ## Estimated Code Review Effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~25 minutes

🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
pkg/controller/runtimeextractor/resources/daemonset.go (1)
`132-147`: _🏗️ Heavy lift_ **Modern TLS profile won’t downgrade `--tls-min-version` via empty cipher fallback** In `pkg/controller/runtimeextractor/resources/daemonset.go`, the `supportedCiphers`-empty path reassigns `profileSpec` to `TLSProfileIntermediateType`, which would change `--tls-min-version`. However, for the built-in `TLSProfileModernType`, this fallback isn’t reachable: `TLSProfileModernType` uses `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` / `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` / `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`, `library-go`’s `OpenSSLToIANACipherSuites` maps them 1:1, and `crypto.CipherSuite` accepts them—so the Modern case stays at `VersionTLS13` (covered by `Test_kubeRBACProxyTLSArgs`). Keep in mind the downgrade still can happen if `supportedCiphers` becomes empty due to an unsupported Custom/invalid cipher list. Consider falling back only the cipher list while preserving the originally resolved `MinTLSVersion`.
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@pkg/controller/runtimeextractor/resources/daemonset.go` around lines 132 - 147, The fallback branch currently replaces profileSpec with TLSProfileIntermediateType which unintentionally changes the resolved MinTLSVersion; modify the empty supportedCiphers handling so it only replaces the cipher list while preserving the original profileSpec.MinTLSVersion (i.e., capture the originalMin := profileSpec.MinTLSVersion before overriding cipher names and use originalMin when building the returned args), keep using crypto.OpenSSLToIANACipherSuites and crypto.CipherSuite to rebuild supportedCiphers, and ensure the returned "--tls-min-version=" uses the preserved originalMinTLSVersion rather than the intermediate profileSpec.MinTLSVersion. ```
